lessons.title: ಸ್ವರಗಳು · Vowels
lessons.subtitle: Kannada vowels — the ಸ್ವರಗಳು, 14 in all
lessons.content:
# ಸ್ವರಗಳು (Vowels)

Kannada uses the **Kannada script**. Its vowels are called **ಸ್ವರಗಳು** —
literally "self-sounding" letters. There are **14 of them**, and each one
can be short or long. Getting the short/long difference right early will
make every later word easier.

## The 14 Vowels

| Vowel | Roman | Example word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| ಅ | a | ಅಮ್ಮ | mother |
| ಆ | ā | ಆಕಾಶ | sky |
| ಇ | i | ಇಲ್ಲಿ | here |
| ಈ | ī | ಈಗ | now |
| ಉ | u | ಉಣ್ಣು | eat |
| ಊ | ū | ಊಟ | meal |
| ಋ | r̥ | ಋಷಿ | sage |
| ಎ | e | ಎಲ್ಲೆ | boundary |
| ಏ | ē | ಏಳು | seven / rise |
| ಐ | ai | ಐದು | five |
| ಒ | o | ಒಂದು | one |
| ಓ | ō | ಓಡು | run |
| ಔ | au | ಔಷಧ | medicine |
| ಅಂ | aṃ | ಅಂದು | that day |

> ಅಂ (anusvāra) and ಅಃ (visarga) appear at the end of the vowel list but
> behave as nasal/final marks rather than full vowels.

## Short vs long

Length changes meaning, not just sound: **ಕವಿ** (kavi, poet) vs
**ಕಾವಿ** (kāvi, ochre); **ಬೆಳೆ** (beḷe, crop) vs **ಬೇಳೆ** (bēḷe, lentils).
Listen for the *held* vowel — that is the long one.

## Where you'll see them

Every Kannada letter hangs from a horizontal bar called the **ಶಿರೆ**
(headstroke) — writing practice always starts at the top stroke and
sweeps down. Vowels standing alone (as in the table) are used at the
start of words or after another vowel; inside words, vowels attach to
consonants as **matras** (next lessons).
## Mini-practice

Cover the Roman column and read: ಅನ್ನ (anna, cooked rice), ಈಗ (īga,
now), ಐದು (aidu, five), ಓಡು (ōḍu, run), ಔಷಧ (auṣadha, medicine).
Then reverse: say "aa" as in father → which letter? (ಆ). The nasal ಅಂ
appears in ಅಂದು and ಸಂಗೀತ (saṃgīta, music). Five minutes now saves
hours later.

lessons.title: ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು · Consonants
lessons.subtitle: The structured consonant grid and the sounds Kannada is known for
lessons.content:
# ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು (Consonants)

Kannada consonants (**ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು**) are arranged in a tidy grid by
*where* the tongue is and *how* much air flows. Every consonant here
carries a built-in **ಅ** sound unless marked otherwise: **ಕ** is read
"ka", **ಗ** is "ga".

## The velar to labial grid

| | Voiceless | Voiceless aspirated | Voiced | Voiced aspirated | Nasal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Velar | ಕ ka | ಖ kha | ಗ ga | ಘ gha | ಙ ṅa |
| Palatal | ಚ ca | ಛ cha | ಜ ja | ಝ jha | ಞ nya |
| Retroflex | ಟ ṭa | ಠ ṭha | ಡ ḍa | ಢ ḍha | ಣ ṇa |
| Dental | ತ ta | ಥ tha | ದ da | ಧ dha | ನ na |
| Labial | ಪ pa | ಫ pha | ಬ ba | ಭ bha | ಮ ma |

## The "others" row

| Letter | Roman | Note |
|---|---|---|
| ಯ | ya | glide, very common |
| ರ | ra | often curls below in combos |
| ಱ | ṟa | old alveolar r (rare today) |
| ಲ | la | dental l |
| ಳ | ḷa | retroflex l — Kannada loves this sound |
| ವ | va | v/w |
| ಶ ಷ ಸ | śa ṣa sa | three s-like letters |
| ಹ | ha | h |

## Retroflex vs dental

**ಟ** (ṭa) is made with the tongue *curled back*; **ತ** (ta) with the
tongue *at the teeth*. Words borrow the difference to mean different
things: **ಕಣ್ಣು** (kaṇṇu, eye) vs **ಕನ್ನಡ** (kannaḍa, the language
itself!). Train your ear on that curl — it is the signature sound of
Dravidian languages.
## Mini-practice

Read aloud: ಕಮಲ (kamala, lotus), ಗಜ (gaja, elephant), ಮಳೆ (maḷe,
rain), ಹಳ್ಳಿ (haḷḷi, village), ವಾರ (vāra, week), ಸರ (sara, flow).
Spot the retroflex: ಳ in ಮಳೆ and ಹಳ್ಳಿ is the curled one — it
contrasts with dental ಲ (hear ಕಮಲ vs ಮಳೆ). Say both back to back and
feel the tongue jump.

lessons.title: ಮಾತ್ರೆಗಳು · Vowel Signs
lessons.subtitle: How vowels attach to consonants as live signs (ಗುಣಿತಾಕ್ಷರ)
lessons.content:
# ಮಾತ್ರೆಗಳು (Vowel Signs)

A bare consonant like **ಕ** says "ka". To change that vowel, Kannada
attaches a **vowel sign** (ಮಾತ್ರೆ). The consonant + sign unit is called a
**ಗುಣಿತಾಕ್ಷರ** — a "developed letter".

## The pattern, using ಕ

| Sign | Result | Sound |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | ಕ | ka |
| ಾ | ಕಾ | kā |
| ಿ | ಕಿ | ki |
| ೀ | ಕೀ | kī |
| ು | ಕು | ku |
| ೂ | ಕೂ | kū |
| ೆ | ಕೆ | ke |
| ೇ | ಕೇ | kē |
| ೈ | ಕೈ | kai |
| ೊ | ಕೊ | ko |
| ೋ | ಕೋ | kō |
| ೌ | ಕೌ | kau |

## The two sides matter

Notice that **ಿ** attaches on the *left* of the consonant even though it
is spoken *after* it: **ಕಿ** = ಕ + ಿ, read "ki". This is the single most
confusing thing for new readers — the sign order and the reading order
disagree. Practise reading **ಕಿವಿ** (kivi, ear) and **ನದಿ** (nadi, river)
slowly.

## The killer u

The vowels ಉ/ಊ often appear as **alternate forms** that hook *below* the
letter (e.g. **ಕು** has a rounded under-hook). Same sound, different
shape — learn each high-frequency consonant's forms by sight.

> Reading strategy: find the headstroke first, count the verticals, then
> read left → right. Word: **ಗುಡಿ** (guḍi, hut), **ಕೋಣೆ** (kōṇe, room).
## Mini-practice

Read: ಕಿವಿ (kivi, ear), ಗುಡಿ (guḍi, hut), ಕೋಣೆ (kōṇe, room), ನದಿ
(nadi, river), ಮೂರು (mūru, three). Then write ಹೆಸರು (hesaru, name)
letter by letter: ಹೆ-ಸ-ರು — three consonants, three different matras
(ೆ, none, ು). If you can do ಹೆಸರು you can do half of Kannada.

lessons.title: ವಟ್ಟಕ್ಷರ · Conjuncts
lessons.subtitle: Subjoined letters (vattakshara) — two consonants, one cluster
lessons.content:
# ವಟ್ಟಕ್ಷರ (Conjunct Consonants)

When two consonants meet with no vowel between them, Kannada usually
shows the second one **dwarfed and pushed below** the first. That
subjoined letter is **ವಟ್ಟಕ್ಷರ** (vattakshara). The cluster **ನ್ನ** in
**ಕನ್ನಡ** (kannaḍa) is exactly this: ನ + ನ with the second ನ tucked
below.

## Common subjoined forms

| Cluster | Word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ನ್ನ | ಕನ್ನಡ | Kannada |
| ಮ್ಮ | ಅಮ್ಮ | mother |
| ಲ್ಲ | ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ | silver |
| ರ್ವ | ಸರ್ವ | all |
| ರ್ಯ | ಧೈರ್ಯ | courage |
| ತ್ರ | ಮಂತ್ರ | chant |
| ಕ್ಕ | ಹಕ್ಕ | right (claim) |
| ಟ್ಟ | ಕಟ್ಟು | to build/tie |

## Half-forms with the pullika

The little diagonal **ಪುಳ್ಳಿ (pulli-like virama)** written as **್**
kills a consonant's vowel: **ಕ್** is just "k". So **ಉತ್ತರ** (uttara,
north) = ಉ + ತ್ + ತ + ರ. If you see **್**, the vowel is gone.

## Reading drill

Try these, top to bottom: **ಸ್ವಾಗತ** (svāgata, welcome),
**ಗ್ರಂಥ** (grantha, book), **ಪ್ರೀತಿ** (prīti, love),
**ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ** (saṃskṛti, culture).

> Speed tip: you do NOT parse every dwarf letter consciously. Frequent
> clusters (ನ್ನ, ಮ್ಮ, ಲ್ಲ, ಟ್ಟ) become single sight-shapes — exactly like
> English "th". practise ten minutes a day and they fuse.
## Mini-practice

Read: ಕನ್ನಡ, ಅಮ್ಮ, ಧೈರ್ಯ, ಸ್ವಾಗತ, ಪ್ರೀತಿ, ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ. Then split them:
ಕ+ನ್+ನ+ಡ, ಅ+ಮ್+ಮ, ಧ+ಯ (long) + ರ್+ಯ. Count how many dwarf letters you
found (five across all six words). Sight-shapes achieved — this is the
lesson where Kannada starts looking like words, not puzzles.

lessons.title: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ · Greetings
lessons.subtitle: Namaskāra and the everyday hello in Karnataka
lessons.content:
# ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ (Greetings)

The all-purpose Kannada greeting is **ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ** (namaskāra) — polite,
safe, correct at any time of day, with anyone. Folded hands optional but
common. A warmer rural hello is **ಯಾಕೋ** (a friendly "hey, what's up")
among close friends only.

## Core greeting set

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ | namaskāra | hello / greetings |
| ಶುಭೋದಯ | śubhōdaya | good morning |
| ಶುಭ ರಾತ್ರಿ | śubha rātri | good night |
| ಹೋಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ | hōgi baruttēne | "I'll go and come back" (goodbye) |
| ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು | dhanyavādagaḷu | thank you |
| ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ | kṣamisi | sorry / excuse me |

## Asking how someone is

- **ಹೇಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ?** (hēgiddīrā?) — How are you? (respectful plural)
- **ಹೇಗಿದ್ದೀಯ?** (hēgiddīya?) — How are you? (to a friend/child)
- Answer: **ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೇನೆ** (cennāgiddēne) — I'm well.
- Or **ಸರಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದೇನೆ** (sariyāgiddēne) — I'm fine/okay.

## The goodbye that means "see you"

Kannada speakers rarely say a final "goodbye". **ಹೋಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ**
literally means "I will go and come back" — leaving is always framed as
returning. Reply with **ಬನ್ನಿ ಬನ್ನಿ** (come, come) or simply
**ಸರಿ** (sari, okay).

> Culture note: elders are addressed with the plural/respect forms
> throughout — **ನೀವು** (you-respectful), never **ನೀನು** (you-intimate),
> unless family or very close friends.
## Mini-practice

Build the greeting exchange out loud: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ! → ಹೇಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ? →
ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೇನೆ, ನೀವು? → ಸರಿ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು! That is a complete,
polite, natural opening — memorise it as one breath. Then the closer:
ಹೋಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ. Six sentences; you can already greet the whole
state.

lessons.title: ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು · Introductions
lessons.subtitle: Saying who you are and asking someone's name
lessons.content:
# ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು (Introductions)

## Saying your name

**ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ರವಿ.** (Nanna hesaru Ravi.) — My name is Ravi.

Break it down: **ನನ್ನ** (my) + **ಹೆಸರು** (name). To ask someone else:
**ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು?** (Nimma hesaru ēnu?) — What is your name? (respectful)
or **ನಿನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು?** (Ninna hesaru ēnu?) — to a friend.

## Where you're from

- **ನಾನು ಭಾರತದಿಂದ ಬಂದವನು.** — I come from India. (said by a man)
- **ನಾನು ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನವಳು.** — I'm from Bengaluru. (said by a woman)
- Pattern: **ನಾನು ___ ನವನು / ನವಳು** (I am from ___ / native of ___).
  The ending marks gender: **-ನವನು** masculine, **-ನವಳು** feminine.

## Handy intro lines

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ನನ್ನ ಪರಿಚಯ | nanna paricaya | my introduction |
| ನನಗೆ ಸಂತೋಷ | nanage santōṣa | nice to meet (lit. joy to me) |
| ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ? | nīvu elliṃda? | where are you from? |
| ನಾನು ಕನ್ನಡ ಕಲಿಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ | nānu kannaḍa kaliyuttiddēne | I am learning Kannada |

## The magic phrase

**ನನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಸರಿ ಇಲ್ಲ** (Nanna kannaḍa svalpa sari illa) —
"My Kannada isn't quite right." People instantly slow down, smile, and
help. Then: **ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ** (nidhānavāgi mātanāḍi) —
"please speak slowly". These two sentences open more doors than perfect
grammar ever will.
## Mini-practice

Fill in and say: ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ___. ನಾನು ___ ನವನು/ನವಳು. ನನಗೆ ಸಂತೋಷ!
Then ask: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರು ಏನು? ನೀವು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ? Keep the respect endings
(-ನವರು for a respected person: ಅವರು ಭಾರತದವರು — they are from India).
Practise with a mirror; introduce yourself three times.

lessons.title: ಕುಟುಂಬ · Family
lessons.subtitle: The age-marked kinship words Kannada families run on
lessons.content:
# ಕುಟುಂಬ (Family)

Kannada kinship words encode **relative age**, not just relation. A
brother is one of two words depending on whether he is older or younger
than you. There is no single neutral "brother".

## The core family

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ಅಮ್ಮ | amma | mother |
| ಅಪ್ಪ | appa | father |
| ಅಣ್ಣ | aṇṇa | elder brother |
| ತಮ್ಮ | tamma | younger brother |
| ಅಕ್ಕ | akka | elder sister |
| ತಂಗಿ | taṅgi | younger sister |
| ಅಜ್ಜ | ajja | grandfather |
| ಅಜ್ಜಿ | ajji | grandmother |
| ಮಗ | maga | son |
| ಮಗಳು | magaḷu | daughter |

## Using them as address

These words double as **forms of address** — you call your elder brother
**ಅಣ್ಣ** to his face, and a friendly shopkeeper's wife **ಅಕ್ಕ**. Even
strangers: an auto driver may be **ಅಣ್ಣ**, a vegetable seller
**ಅಕ್ಕ/ಅಮ್ಮ** depending on age.

## Sentences

- **ಇದು ನನ್ನ ಅಣ್ಣ.** — This is my elder brother.
- **ನನ್ನ ಅಕ್ಕ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕಿ.** — My elder sister is a teacher.
- **ನನ್ನ ಕುಟುಂಬ ದೊಡ್ಡದು.** — My family is big.
- **ನನಗೆ ಒಬ್ಬ ತಮ್ಮ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ.** — I have one younger brother.

> Note the respect order at the dinner table too — elders are served
> first, and the words for aunt/uncle (ಚಿಕ್ಕಪ್ಪ, ದೊಡ್ಡಮ್ಮ…) keep the same
> older/younger logic on the parent's side.
## Mini-practice

Map YOUR family: ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಪ್ಪ, elder/younger brothers and sisters with
ಅಣ್ಣ/ತಮ್ಮ/ಅಕ್ಕ/ತಂಗಿ, then grandparents ಅಜ್ಜ/ಅಜ್ಜಿ. Say two sentences:
ಇದು ನನ್ನ ___. ನನಗೆ ___ ಇದ್ದಾನೆ/ಇದ್ದಾಳೆ (I have a brother/sister).
Notice how the kinship word itself tells the listener who is older —
no pronoun needed.

lessons.title: ಎಣಿಕೆ · Numbers
lessons.subtitle: Kannada numerals ೦–೯ and counting to one hundred
lessons.content:
# ಎಣಿಕೆ (Numbers)

## The numerals

| Digit | Kannada | Name | Digit | Kannada | Name |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | ೦ | ಶೂನ್ಯ | 5 | ೫ | ಐದು |
| 1 | ೧ | ಒಂದು | 6 | ೬ | ಆರು |
| 2 | ೨ | ಎರಡು | 7 | ೭ | ಏಳು |
| 3 | ೩ | ಮೂರು | 8 | ೮ | ಎಂಟು |
| 4 | ೪ | ನಾಲ್ಕು | 9 | ೯ | ಒಂಬತ್ತು |

Bus boards and old shop bills use these digits; phones and new signage
often use 0–9. Learn both shapes together.

## 11 to 100

- 11 **ಹನ್ನೊಂದು** (hannond), 12 **ಹನ್ನೆರಡು**, 20 **ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು** (ippattu),
  30 **ಮೂವತ್ತು** (mūvattu), 40 **ನಲವತ್ತು** (nalavattu),
  50 **ಐವತ್ತು** (aivattu), 100 **ನೂರು** (nūru).
- Pattern for 21+: **ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತ್ ಒಂದು** → written **ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದು**
  (ippattoṃda) — twenty-one, literally "twenty-one".

## Money and age

- **ಎಷ್ಟು?** (eṣṭu?) — how much? The first market word you need.
- **ಐವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ** — fifty rupees.
- Age: **ನನಗೆ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ವರ್ಷ ವಯಸ್ಸಾಗಿದೆ** — I am twenty years old.
  (Lit. "to me twenty years of age have happened.")

> Kannada counting is a *systems* language: 10 **ಹತ್ತು**, and the tens
> words carry old forms (ippattu, mūvattu…) that just need memorising —
> they are irregular the way English "eleven, twelve" are.
## Mini-practice

Count aloud ೧→೧೦, then jump the tens: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು, ಮೂವತ್ತು, ನಲವತ್ತು,
ಐವತ್ತು, ನೂರು. Market drill: ಎಷ್ಟು? → ಐವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ → ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ
ಮಾಡಿ! (reduce a little!) → ಸರಿ. You have just haggled in Kannada —
the national sport of every Bengaluru market.

lessons.title: ಸರಳ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳು · Simple Sentences
lessons.subtitle: SOV word order and the verb 'to be' — your first real sentences
lessons.content:
# ಸರಳ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳು (Simple Sentences)

Kannada is **SOV**: Subject → Object → Verb. The verb parks at the end,
always. English "I eat rice" becomes "I rice eat".

## Word order

- **ನಾನು ಅನ್ನ ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — I eat rice. (I rice eat)
- **ಅವನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದುತ್ತಾನೆ.** — He reads a book.
- **ಮಗು ಹಾಲು ಕುಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.** — The child drinks milk.

## The "to be" verb

**ಇರು** (to be) appears as **ಇದ್ದೇನೆ / ಇದ್ದಾನೆ / ಇದ್ದಾಳೆ / ಇದೆ**:

- **ನಾನು ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೇನೆ.** — I am at home.
- **ಅವನು ಶಾಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದಾನೆ.** — He is at school.
- **ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಇದೆ.** — The book is on the table.

## Location glue: -ಅಲ್ಲಿ

**ಮನೆ + ಅಲ್ಲಿ → ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ** (in the house); **ಊರಲ್ಲಿ** (in town);
**ಬೀದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ** (on the street). "On/above" is **ಮೇಲೆ**, "under" is
**ಕೆಳಗೆ**, "near" is **ಹತ್ತಿರ**.

## Three more everyday verbs

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ಹೋಗು | hōgu | go |
| ಬಾ | bā | come |
| ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳು | kuḷitukoḷḷu | sit (down) |

**ನಾನು ಊರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ** — I am going to town. (**-ಗೆ** = "to".)
## Mini-practice

Swap nouns in the frames: ನಾನು ___ ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ (ಊಟ/ಹಣ್ಣು/ದೋಸೆ).
ಅವನು ___ ಓದುತ್ತಾನೆ (ಪುಸ್ತಕ/ಪತ್ರಿಕೆ). ಪುಸ್ತಕ ___ ಇದೆ (ಮೇಜಿನ ಮೇಲೆ/ಮಣೆಯ
ಮೇಲೆ). Remember the ending changes with the pronoun — ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ
(I), ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾನೆ (he), ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾಳೆ (she), ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ (they/resp).

lessons.title: ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು · Questions
lessons.subtitle: What, who, where, when — the four question words that unlock talk
lessons.content:
# ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು (Questions)

Kannada question words stay **in place** — no word shuffling. "You are
going where?" is exactly how it works.

## The question words

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| ಏನು | ēnu | what | ಇದು ಏನು? — What is this? |
| ಯಾರು | yāru | who | ಅವರು ಯಾರು? — Who is that? |
| ಎಲ್ಲಿ | elli | where | ಬಸ್ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? — Where is the bus? |
| ಯಾವಾಗ | yāvāga | when | ಬರುವಿರಾ? ಯಾವಾಗ? — When are you coming? |
| ಎಷ್ಟು | eṣṭu | how much | ಎಷ್ಟು ಬೆಲೆ? — How much is it? |
| ಯಾವ | yāva | which | ಯಾವ ಊರು? — Which town? |

## Yes / no questions

Add **-ಆ?** to the last word and raise the tone:
**ನೀವು ಬರುವಿರಾ?** (nīvu baruvirā?) — Are you coming?
**ಸರಿಯಾ?** (sariyā?) — Is it okay?

## The all-purpose answers

- **ಹೌದು** (haudu) — yes. **ಅಲ್ಲ / ಇಲ್ಲ** (alla / illa) — no / not.
- **ಸರಿ** (sari) — okay/fine — the most used word in Karnataka, honestly.
- **ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ** (gottilla) — I don't know. Save this one; you'll use it.

## Politeness tap

Soften a question with **ಪ್ಲೀಸ್**-free Kannada: **ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ** (one
moment), **ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ** (excuse me) before asking a stranger. A question
wrapped in ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ never sounds rude.
## Mini-practice

Answer, don't just ask: ಇದು ಏನು? → ಇದು ಪುಸ್ತಕ. ಬಸ್ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? → ಅಲ್ಲಿ!
ಯಾವಾಗ ಬರುವಿರಾ? → ಈಗಲೇ (right now). ಎಷ್ಟು ಬೆಲೆ? → ನಲವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ.
Question words stay put, answers slot into the same hole — practise
the pair, not just the question.

lessons.title: ನಿಷೇಧ · Negation
lessons.subtitle: ಇಲ್ಲ, ಅಲ್ಲ, -ಅಲ್ಲ — the three no's and when each applies
lessons.content:
# ನಿಷೇಧ (Negation)

Kannada splits "no" into jobs. Pick the right one and sentences click.

## 1. ಇಲ್ಲ — "there isn't / I don't have"

- **ಹಣ ಇಲ್ಲ.** — There is no money.
- **ನನಗೆ ಸಮಯ ಇಲ್ಲ.** — I have no time. (Lit. "to me time is-not")
- **ಇಲ್ಲ, ಬೇಡ.** — No, (I) don't want.

## 2. ಅಲ್ಲ — "it is not" (identity)

- **ಇದು ಹಾಲು ಅಲ್ಲ, ನೀರು.** — This is not milk, (it is) water.
- **ನಾನು ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್ ಅಲ್ಲ.** — I am not a doctor.

## 3. Verb negation — the -ಅಲ್ಲ / -ಇಲ್ಲ endings

Verbs negate by suffix: **ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ** (I go) → **ಹೋಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ**
(I won't go) / habitual **ಹೋಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ**; simple past negative uses
**-ಅಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲ**: **ಹೋಗಲಿಲ್ಲ** (did not go).

| Positive | Negative | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ಗೊತ್ತು | ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ | know / don't know |
| ಇಷ್ಟ | ಇಷ್ಟವಿಲ್ಲ | like / don't like |
| ಬೇಕು | ಬೇಡ | want / don't want |
| ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ | ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ | can be done / can't be done |

> **ಬೇಡ** (bēḍa) is the polite "no thank you" — at a shop, **ಬೇಡ ಸಾರ್**
> ("no, thanks") with a small head shake closes any sales pitch kindly.
## Mini-practice

Pick the right no: water absent? → ನೀರು ಇಲ್ಲ. Not a doctor? → ನಾನು
ಡಾಕ್ಟರ್ ಅಲ್ಲ. Don't know? → ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. Don't want? → ಬೇಡ. Four no's
with four jobs — ಇಲ್ಲ for absence, ಅಲ್ಲ for identity, ಬೇಡ for
refusal, ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ for knowledge. Zero confusion now.

lessons.title: ದಿನಚರಿ · Daily Routine
lessons.subtitle: Telling what you do every day — clocks, meals, and the work verb
lessons.content:
# ದಿನಚರಿ (Daily Routine)

## Clock times

- **ಈಗ ಎಷ್ಟು ಗಂಟೆ?** — What time is it now?
- **ಆರು ಗಂಟೆಯಾಗಿದೆ.** — It is six o'clock.
- Morning **ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ**, afternoon **ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ**, evening **ಸಂಜೆ**,
  night **ರಾತ್ರಿ**. **ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆ** — seven in the morning.

## A day, narrated

- **ನಾನು ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಆರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಏಳುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — I wake at six in the morning.
- **ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — I drink coffee. (Bengaluru approves.)
- **ಎಂಟರಿಗೆ ಕೆಲಸಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — At eight I go to work.
- **ರಾತ್ರಿ ಹತ್ತರಿಗೆ ಮಲಗುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — At ten at night I sleep.

## Meal words

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meal |
|---|---|---|
| ತಿಂಡಿ | tiṃdi | breakfast/snack |
| ಊಟ | ūṭa | lunch/full meal |
| ತಿಂಡಿ (evening) | — | tiffin, evening snack |
| ಅಹಾರ | ahāra | food (formal) |

**ಊಟ ಆಯಿತಾ?** — Is lunch done/ready? **ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿದೆ!** — It's tasty!

## Every-day verbs to chain

ಏಳು (wake) → ಕುಡಿ (drink) → ಹೋಗು (go) → ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡು (work) →
ಬಾ (come back) → ತಿನ್ನು (eat) → ಮಲಗು (sleep). String five of them with
times and you have a full minute of natural Kannada.
## Mini-practice

Narrate YOUR day in five sentences: ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ___ ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಏಳುತ್ತೇನೆ.
ಚಹಾ/ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯುತ್ತೇನೆ. ___ ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಕೆಲಸಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ. ಸಂಜೆ ___ ಇರುತ್ತೇನೆ.
ರಾತ್ರಿ ___ ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಮಲಗುತ್ತೇನೆ. Time words + verbs = a full spoken
routine. Record yourself once; listen for the verb at the end.

lessons.title: ಸರ್ವನಾಮಗಳು · Pronouns
lessons.subtitle: The nine pronouns and the respect line you must not cross
lessons.content:
# ಸರ್ವನಾಮಗಳು (Pronouns)

## The set

| Kannada | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ನಾನು | nānu | I |
| ನೀನು | nīnu | you (intimate) |
| ನೀವು | nīvu | you (respectful/plural) |
| ಅವನು | avanu | he (close) |
| ಅವಳು | avaḷu | she (close) |
| ಅದು | adu | it |
| ನಾವು | nāvu | we |
| ಅವರು | avaru | they / he-she (respectful) |
| ಅವು | avu | they (things) |

## The respect line

Use **ನೀವು** with strangers, elders, teachers, customers — everyone
outside your closest circle. **ನೀನು** is for children, younger siblings,
close friends. Referring *about* a respected person? Use **ಅವರು**
("they") — the respectful plural doubles as honorific "he/she".

## Gender is natural, not grammatical

Tables, books, cities are all **ಅದು/ಅವು** (it/they) — Kannada has no
masculine-feminine *grammar* for objects. Only people take ಅವನು/ಅವಳು.
This makes noun gender — the nightmare of Hindi learners — a non-issue
here.

## Verb agreement preview

The pronoun picks the verb ending:
ನಾನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ (I do) / ನೀನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀಯ / ಅವನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ /
ಅವಳು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾಳೆ / ನಾವು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇವೆ / ನೀವು ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀರಿ / ಅವರು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾರೆ.
One verb, seven endings — you already know the pattern words.
## Mini-practice

Conjugate ಓದು (read) across the set: ನಾನು ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ, ನೀನು ಓದುತ್ತೀಯ,
ಅವನು ಓದುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಅವಳು ಓದುತ್ತಾಳೆ, ನಾವು ಓದುತ್ತೇವೆ, ನೀವು ಓದುತ್ತೀರಿ,
ಅವರು ಓದುತ್ತಾರೆ. Say it as a rhythm chant — the endings are a song.
Then swap the verb to ಬರು (come): ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ… same endings.

lessons.title: ಕಾಲಗಳು · Tenses
lessons.subtitle: Present, past, future with one verb — ಮಾಡು (do) as the pattern
lessons.content:
# ಕಾಲಗಳು (Tenses)

## The three-time map, using ಮಾಡು (do)

| Tense | I-form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Present | ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ / ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ | I am doing / I do |
| Past | ಮಾಡಿದೆನು / ಮಾಡಿದೆ | I did |
| Future | ಮಾಡುವೆನು / ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ (fut.) | I will do |

Present takes **-ಉತ್ತ-**, past takes **-ಇದ್-**, future takes **-ಉವ-**,
then the person ending slots in. Watch it with ಹೋಗು (go):
ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ / ಹೋದೆನು / ಹೋಗುವೆನು.

## Past forms twist

Strong verbs often change inside the past: **ಕೊಡು** (give) →
**ಕೊಟ್ಟೆನು** (gave); **ತಗೊಳ್ಳು** (take) → **ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡೆನು** (took);
**ಬಾ** (come) → **ಬಂದೆನು** (came); **ಹೋಗು** → **ಹೋದೆನು** (went).
Learn the past form *with* the verb, like a second word.

## Daily three

- **ನಾನು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಓದುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — I read every day.
- **ನಿನ್ನೆ ನಾನು ಚಿತ್ರ ನೋಡಿದೆನು.** — Yesterday I watched a movie.
- **ನಾಳೆ ನಾನು ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುವೆನು.** — Tomorrow I will go to Mysuru.

Time words do half the tense work: **ಇಂದು** (today), **ನಿನ್ನೆ**
(yesterday), **ನಾಳೆ** (tomorrow), **ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ** (every day).
## Mini-practice

Past-form pairs to memorise as words: ಹೋಗು→ಹೋದೆನು, ಬಾ→ಬಂದೆನು,
ಕೊಡು→ಕೊಟ್ಟೆನು, ತಿನ್ನು→ತಿಂದೆನು, ನೋಡು→ನೋಡಿದೆನು. Build: ನಿನ್ನೆ ನಾನು
ಊರಿಗೆ ಹೋದೆನು. ನಾಳೆ ನಾನು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಕೊಡುವೆನು. Three tenses, one verb at a
time — the pattern does the rest.

lessons.title: ವಿಭಕ್ತಿ · Case Endings
lessons.subtitle: To, from, with, in — the suffixes that do prepositions' job
lessons.content:
# ವಿಭಕ್ತಿ (Case Endings)

Kannada has no prepositions. Instead, the noun wears a **case ending**
at its end. Learn six endings and you can build location, direction and
companionship sentences all day.

## The big six

| Ending | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| -ಗೆ | to | ಮನೆಗೆ (home-to) |
| -ಇಂದ | from | ಊರಿಂದ (town-from) |
| -ಅಲ್ಲಿ | in/at | ಶಾಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ (in school) |
| -ಜೊತೆ | with | ಸ್ನೇಹಿತರ ಜೊತೆ (with friends) |
| -ನ / -ಅವರ | 's (possessive) | ರವಿಯ ಪುಸ್ತಕ (Ravi's book) |
| -ಅನ್ನು | object marker | ಅನ್ನವನ್ನು ತಿನ್ನು (eat the rice) |

## Sandhi glue

Endings fuse with the noun: ಮನೆ + ಅಲ್ಲಿ → **ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ** (a -ಯ- slips
in); ಶಾಲೆ + ಗೆ → **ಶಾಲೆಗೆ**. Expect a connective ಯ/ವ sound with
vowel-ending nouns — it is regular, not chaos.

## Sentences to steal

- **ನಾನು ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತೇನೆ.** — I'm going to Bengaluru.
- **ಅವರು ದೆಹಲಿಯಿಂದ ಬಂದರು.** — They came from Delhi.
- **ನಾನು ಅಪ್ಪನ ಜೊತೆ ಊರಲ್ಲಿ ಇದ್ದೆ.** — I was in town with dad.
- **ಇದು ಅಜ್ಜಿಯ ಮನೆ.** — This is grandmother's house.

> The object marker **-ಅನ್ನು** is optional with indefinite things
> (ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಓದು) but expected with definite ones (ಪುಸ್ತಕವನ್ನು ಓದು).
## Mini-practice

Slot the endings: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು___ ಹೋಗು (→ -ಗೆ), ದೆಹಲಿ___ ಬಾ (→ -ಇಂದ),
ಶಾಲೆ___ ಇರು (→ -ಅಲ್ಲಿ), ಗೆಳೆಯ___ ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ? — ಸ್ನೇಹಿತರ ಜೊತೆ (with
friends, → -ಜೊತೆ), ರವಿ___ ಪುಸ್ತಕ (→ -ಯ: ರವಿಯ ಪುಸ್ತಕ). Watch the glue
ಯ/ವ appear with vowel-ending nouns.

lessons.title: ಗೌರವ · Politeness
lessons.subtitle: Plurals of respect, the -ರು rule, and softening words
lessons.content:
# ಗೌರವ (Politeness & Honorifics)

## The -ರು respect rule

To respect a person, Kannada adds **-ರು** (or swaps in the plural verb):
**ರವಿ ಬಂದಾನೆ** (Ravi came) → **ರವಿಗಳು ಬಂದರು** or better **ರವಿ ಅವರು
ಬಂದರು**. The **-ಅವರು** attach (as in **ರವಿಯವರು**) is the classic
polite style — you will hear it in every announcement and speech.

## Respect in verbs

| Intimate | Respectful | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ಬಾ | ಬನ್ನಿ | come |
| ಕೂರು | ಕೂರಿ / ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ | sit |
| ಹೇಳು | ಹೇಳಿ | say/tell |
| ಇರು | ಇರಿ | stay/be |

A shop line: **ಬನ್ನಿ, ಕೂರಿ, ಏನು ಬೇಕು?** — Come, sit, what do you need?

## Softeners

- **ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ** — one moment (please wait a bit)
- **ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು** — please (formal, announcements)
- **ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ** — a little (a little slowly, a little less)
- **ನಿಧಾನ** — slowly/patiently — **ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಮಾತನಾಡಿ** = speak slowly

## Address titles

**ಅಣ್ಣ/ಅಕ್ಕ** (elder brother/sister) for peers; **ಅಂಕಲ್/ಆಂಟಿ** (from
English) are completely natural in cities; **ಸಾರ್/ಮೇಡಂ** in offices.
**ಅವರು** always for third-person respect. Mixing one ಅಕ್ಕ into a
sentence instantly warms it up.
## Mini-practice

Convert to respectful: ಬಾ → ಬನ್ನಿ. ಕುಳಿತುಕೋ → ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ. ಹೇಳು →
ಹೇಳಿ. ತಿನ್ನು → ತಿನ್ನಿ. Then soften a demand: ನೀರು ಕೊಡು → ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ,
ನೀರು ಕೊಡಿ? Same sentence, new warmth. End with the universal
soother: ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ — there is no rush in Karnataka.

lessons.title: ಸಂಭಾಷಣೆ · Conversations
lessons.subtitle: Two full dialogues — at the market and meeting a friend
lessons.content:
# ಸಂಭಾಷಣೆ (Conversations)

## At the vegetable market

> **ಅಂಗಡಿಯವರು:** ಬನ್ನಿ ಬನ್ನಿ, ಏನು ಬೇಕು?
> **ನೀವು:** ಟೊಮ್ಯಾಟೊ ಎಷ್ಟು?
> **ಅಂಗಡಿಯವರು:** ಕೆಜಿ ನಲವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ.
> **ನೀವು:** ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ!
> **ಅಂಗಡಿಯವರು:** ಸರಿ, ಮೂವತ್ತೈದು ಕೊಡುತ್ತೇನೆ.
> **ನೀವು:** ಸರಿ, ಎರಡು ಕೆಜಿ ಕೊಡಿ.

Translation: "Come! What do you need?" / "How much are tomatoes?" /
"Forty rupees a kilo." / "Make it a little less!" / "Okay, I'll give
thirty-five." / "Fine, give me two kilos."

## Meeting a friend

> **ನೀವು:** ಹಾಯ್ ವಿಜಯ್! ಹೇಗಿದ್ದೀಯ?
> **ವಿಜಯ್:** ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೇನೆ. ನೀನು ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದೀಯ?
> **ನೀವು:** ಪುಸ್ತಕದ ಅಂಗಡಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ.
> **ವಿಜಯ್:** ಸರಿ. ನಾನೂ ಬರುತ್ತೇನೆ!
> **ನೀವು:** ಬಾ ಬಾ, ನಡೆಯೋಣ.

Translation: "Hi Vijay! How are you?" / "I'm well. Where are you
going?" / "To the bookshop." / "Okay, I'll come too!" / "Come on, let's
walk."

## Notice

- **-ತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ** marks the "right now" continuous — ಹೋಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದೇನೆ = am
  going (right now).
- **ನೂ** = "also/too", tagged on: ನಾನೂ = me too.
- **ಬಾ ಬಾ / ನಡೆಯೋಣ** — friendly come-on / let's-go lines, used constantly.
## Mini-practice

Act both roles of the market dialogue from memory, then change the
item: ದ್ರಾಕ್ಷಿ (grapes), ಬಾಳೆಹಣ್ಣು (banana), ಹಾಲು (milk). Change the
numbers too. The frames — ಎಷ್ಟು? / ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ! / ಸರಿ — never
change; only nouns and numerals rotate.

lessons.title: ಪ್ಯಾರಾ ಓದು · Reading Paragraphs
lessons.subtitle: A short postcard from Mysuru — comprehension without fear
lessons.content:
# ಪ್ಯಾರಾ ಓದು (Reading a Paragraph)

## The text

**ನನ್ನ ಮೈಸೂರು ಪ್ರವಾಸ**

ಕಳೆದ ವಾರ ನಾನು ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗಿದ್ದೆ. ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನಿಂದ ಬಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆ.
ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಅರಮನೆ ನೋಡಿದೆ — ಬಹಳ ದೊಡ್ಡದು, ಬಹಳ ಸುಂದರ! ಸಂಜೆ ಚಾಮುಂಡಿ ಬೆಟ್ಟಕ್ಕೆ
ಹೋಗಿ ಊರನ್ನು ನೋಡಿದೆ. ರಸ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮೈಸೂರು ಪಾಕ್ ತಿಂದೆ — ರುಚಿ!

## Sentence by sentence

1. **ಕಳೆದ ವಾರ ನಾನು ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗಿದ್ದೆ.** — Last week I went to Mysuru.
   (ಕಳೆದ = last/past; -ಗೆ = to; ಹೋಗಿದ್ದೆ = went)
2. **ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನಿಂದ ಬಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆ.** — Three hours by bus from
   Bengaluru. (-ಇಂದ = from; -ಅಲ್ಲಿ = in)
3. **ಅರಮನೆ ನೋಡಿದೆ — ಬಹಳ ದೊಡ್ಡದು, ಸುಂದರ!** — Saw the palace — very big,
   beautiful! (ಬಹಳ = very; ದೊಡ್ಡ = big)
4. **ಚಾಮುಂಡಿ ಬೆಟ್ಟಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಿ ಊರನ್ನು ನೋಡಿದೆ.** — Went up Chamundi Hill and
   saw the town. (ಬೆಟ್ಟ = hill)
5. **ಮೈಸೂರು ಪಾಕ್ ತಿಂದೆ — ರುಚಿ!** — Ate Mysore pak — delicious!

## Comprehension check

- How long is the bus ride? **ಮೂರು ಗಂಟೆ** (three hours).
- What did the writer eat? **ಮೈಸೂರು ಪಾಕ್**.
- Two places visited: **ಅರಮನೆ** and **ಚಾಮುಂಡಿ ಬೆಟ್ಟ**.

You just read a real paragraph. Every word in it came from lessons you
have already done — that is the whole point of the ladder.
## Mini-practice

Re-read the Mysuru paragraph aloud twice, then rebuild it from memory
in English→Kannada order: last-week / I / Mysuru-to / went. Where
does the verb land? (At the end — every sentence.) Then change one
detail and re-say it: ಬಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ → ರೈಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ (by train). You are now
editing Kannada, not just reading it.

lessons.title: ಗಾದೆಗಳು · Proverbs
lessons.subtitle: Four Kannada proverbs and the culture inside them
lessons.content:
# ಗಾದೆಗಳು (Proverbs & Culture)

Proverbs (**ಗಾದೆಗಳು**) are grammar, vocabulary and worldview in one
line. Four classics:

## 1. ಮಾತು ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ, ಮೌನ ಬಂಗಾರ

"Speech is silver, silence is gold." — **ಮಾತು** (speech), **ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ**
(silver), **ಮೌನ** (silence), **ಬಂಗಾರ** (gold). Used when someone wisely
holds their tongue.

## 2. ಬಿತ್ತಿದ ಬೀಜ ಮೊಳಕೆಯೊಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ

"The sown seed sprouts." — effort shows its result in time. **ಬಿತ್ತು**
(sow), **ಬೀಜ** (seed), **ಮೊಳಕೆ** (sprout). A farmer's proverb from an
agricultural land — say it to a learner; it applies to you.

## 3. ಇಲ್ಲದ ಮನೆಗೆ ಇರುಳೆ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ

"Like an owl arriving at a house that has nothing." — arriving empty-
handed where nothing exists. **ಇಲ್ಲದ** (not-having), **ಇರುಳೆ** (owl —
ಗೂಬೆ in modern speech). Teaches the classic negative participle **ಇಲ್ಲ+ದ**.

## 4. ಅಪ್ಪ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು ಅಕ್ಷರ, ಅಮ್ಮ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು ಅನ್ನ

"What father says is a letter, what mother says is food." — both
parents' words nourish differently. Notice **ಅಕ್ಷರ** (letter/learning)
and **ಅನ್ನ** (cooked rice/food) — two of Kannada's most culture-loaded
words.

> Proverbs respect word order too — SOV holds inside them. Read each
> one aloud twice; rhythm is half the memory.
## Mini-practice

Match proverb to situation: your friend keeps talking over everyone
(→ ಮಾತು ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ, ಮೌನ ಬಂಗಾರ). You feel your daily practice is slow
(→ ಬಿತ್ತಿದ ಬೀಜ ಮೊಳಕೆಯೊಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ). Say each proverb with the story —
proverbs live as stories, not strings.

lessons.title: ಪುನರ್ವಿಮರ್ಶೆ · Review
lessons.subtitle: Everything from ಅ to ಹ — the full beginner journey in one page
lessons.content:
# ಪುನರ್ವಿಮರ್ಶೆ (Review)

## Script ladder (chapters 1)

- 14 vowels **ಸ್ವರಗಳು**, the consonant grid **ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು**, vowel signs
  **ಮಾತ್ರೆಗಳು**, subjoined clusters **ವಟ್ಟಕ್ಷರ**.
- Reading strategy: headstroke → verticals → left-to-right.
- Sight-clusters to own: ನ್ನ, ಮ್ಮ, ಲ್ಲ, ಟ್ಟ, ರ್ಯ.

## Words you now have (chapter 2)

ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ, ಧನ್ಯವಾದಗಳು, ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ, ಹೇಗಿದ್ದೀರಾ, ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದ್ದೇನೆ,
ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು…, ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಪ್ಪ, ಅಣ್ಣ, ಅಕ್ಕ, ತಮ್ಮ, ತಂಗಿ, ಒಂದು…ಹತ್ತು, ನೂರು,
ಎಷ್ಟು, ರೂಪಾಯಿ.

## Sentences you can build (chapters 3–4)

- SOV with ಇರು: **ನಾನು ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೇನೆ.**
- Questions: **ಇದು ಏನು?** **ಬಸ್ ಎಲ್ಲಿ?** **ಎಷ್ಟು ಬೆಲೆ?**
- Negatives: **ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ**, **ಇದು ಅಲ್ಲ**, **ಬೇಡ**.
- Times: **ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಏಳುತ್ತೇನೆ.**
- Pronouns + endings: ಮಾಡುತ್ತೇನೆ / -ತ್ತೀಯ / -ತ್ತಾನೆ / -ತ್ತಾಳೆ / -ತ್ತೇವೆ /
  -ತ್ತೀರಿ / -ತ್ತಾರೆ.
- Cases: -ಗೆ, -ಇಂದ, -ಅಲ್ಲಿ, -ಜೊತೆ, -ನ, -ಅನ್ನು.

## Self-check questions

1. Write **ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು ___** and finish it with your name.
2. Ask the price of anything: **___ ಎಷ್ಟು?**
3. Say one past-tense sentence with **ಹೋಗು**.
4. Read **ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ**, **ಧೈರ್ಯ**, **ಸ್ವಾಗತ** aloud.

If all four feel easy, you are no longer a beginner in the beginner
chapter sense — the adaptive engine will now push you toward review of
whatever dipped. ಶುಭ! (Good luck!)
## Mini-practice

The four self-check sentences — do them NOW, aloud: 1) ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು
___, 2) ___ ಎಷ್ಟು?, 3) one ಹೋದೆನು-sentence, 4) read ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ, ಧೈರ್ಯ,
ಸ್ವಾಗತ. All smooth? Your practice engine moves to maintenance mode —
short, spaced reviews of exactly what you dipped on.
